newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on weather, Sparks estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on weather, Sparks estimate.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on concerns about adverse weather in U.S. areas where the three main classes of wheat are grown, traders said.

Wet weather in the eastern U.S. Midwest led to concerns about damage to some of the soft red winter crop. Excessive rain and snow in the upper Midwest and northern Plains stirred ideas for delays in seeding spring wheat and a cold snap in the central and southern Plains expected this weekend led to talk about possible damage to the hard red winter wheat crop.
Meteorologists early Friday reported rain in the Ohio River Valley and more than a foot of snow fell from the Dakotas to Wisconsin.
A surge in soybean and corn futures also buoyed wheat futures and an acreage outlook by a key private analytical firm further reinforced the gains.
Traders said Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Co's Friday estimated 1997 U.S. spring wheat acreage at 18.59 million acres, below its previous outlook for 20.312 million.
Wheat closed seven to 10-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 9-1/4 at $3.83-1/4.
Gains in March were limited by news Sri Lanka bought wheat from Argentina and the EU rather than from the U.S. Also a Philippine firm rejected offers on U.S. wheat and soybeans.

The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Friday. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the March closed at 65 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

E.D. and F. Man International and Refco Inc each bought two million bushels of July, traders said. Tenco Inc and Cargill Inc sold one million bushels of July, traders said. FIMAT Futures bought one million bushels of July and sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 26,000 contracts, above the 18,781 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man International sold 500 July $3.80 calls at 17-1/2 cents, Merrill Lynch Futures bought 250 May $4.00 calls at 7-1/2 cents and LIT America sold 200 July $3.90 calls at 17 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 4,237 traded Thursday.
